model.description: joint binomial (product-form multinomial) likelihood, deviance-residual Gauss-Newton
model.spam_note: e0, e1 are EFFECTIVE parameters: the X preparation error in spam_1 (and in control-state-1 preparation) is absorbed into e1; they are not independent detector errors
model.hamiltonian_identifiability: alpha_target and delta identifiable (up to the pi/2 lattice); alpha_control NOT identifiable by design; SPAM contrast and visibility share a weak direction
limitations: Per-site product (independent-readout) likelihood; correlated readout error and crosstalk are only tested through the diagnostics, not modelled.
SX offset and nuisance phase are bounded as in the JS design (+-0.1, +-0.2 rad); a true offset outside the bound is reported at the bound and flagged, not estimated.
Visibility and SPAM contrast share a weak likelihood direction (SPAM circuits pin e0, e1 to about +-0.003 with 384 shots); parameters of interest are not affected at the reported precision.
Profile likelihood is block-conditional: the block's own SPAM parameters are re-optimised, other blocks' weak information about shared SPAM parameters is ignored (slightly conservative).
alpha_control is not identifiable by design; (alpha_target, delta) are identified only modulo the (pi/2, pi/2) lattice, and the reported representative is the smallest-norm one.
Diagnostic thresholds are Bonferroni-calibrated under the Bernoulli model; their false-alarm rates were measured on synthetic data only (receipts) and real hardware noise may differ.
Single dataset: acceptance of any nonzero value additionally requires a fresh, independently shuffled replicate block (decision rule), which this tool cannot supply.

bootstrap.note: joint-bitstring multinomial bootstrap, SPAM circuits resampled and everything refit (global initial grid search each replicate); replicates are mapped to the alias/angle branch closest to the point estimate before percentiles are taken

jacobian.note: Whitened Jacobian of E[1-2b] w.r.t. fitted parameters in natural units (rad, probability). J^T J is the Fisher information; Wald SE = sqrt(diag((J^T J)^-1)).

alias.cz_alias_statement: slope per control state is determined mod pi (m=2 binds; m=8 alone would give pi/4 but is resolved by m=2 only if the m=2 phase noise is well below pi/8); (alpha_t, delta) alias lattice generated by (pi/2, pi/2) and (pi/2, -pi/2)
alias.sx_alias_statement: all m even: exact reflection alias (d, phi0) -> (pi-d, -phi0), outside the +-0.1 design bound; no translation alias (Y axis carries (m+1)d with m+1=1)

sx_block_pair_correlation.threshold_justification: Bonferroni two-sided alpha=0.005 (0.05 split over 10 diagnostic families) over all tested (circuit, pair) cells; z = (n11 - E)/sd under independence given the observed marginals (hypergeometric)

control_marginal_vs_spam.threshold_justification: Fisher exact p < 0.005/12 (Bonferroni, suite-level alpha split over 10 families) AND |difference| > 0.02 (2% population: above typical readout error, enough to mix control-state phases)

prep_phase_block_vs_isolated.threshold_justification: |difference| > 0.05 rad (comparable to the 0.02-0.05 rad effects sought) AND > the Bonferroni z for 6 pairs at alpha 0.005 (SE assumes independent estimates). The intercept is the m=0 phase averaged over control states; the state-dependent half-difference is reported separately and is not an alarm by itself.

leakage_population.threshold_justification: exact conditional trend test p < 0.005/12 (Bonferroni, suite-level alpha split over 10 families) AND |drift m=0->8| > 0.02. Counts are the control's unexpected outcomes (1 for state 0, 0 for state 1). Population change on the control mixes its two phase branches; leakage out of {0,1} shows up as drift or as non-exponential target visibility loss (see relaxation).

relaxation.threshold_justification: weighted fit of ln(visibility) = ln v0 - kappa m with bootstrap SEs; chi-square lack-of-fit p < 0.005/16 (Bonferroni, suite-level alpha split over 10 families) flags non-single-exponential decay. kappa is the apparent per-repetition amplitude decay; it is not separated into T1/Tphi by this plan (1/kappa in repetitions; pass duration_ns for a time conversion). Dof is 2 (SX) or 1 (CZ), so power is limited.

quadrature.threshold_justification: CZ: model-free phase theta_m=atan2(y,x) must be linear in m: R = th8 - 4 th2 + 3 th0 (about the fit) with delta-method SE, Bonferroni over 12 (edge,state); amplitude r=sqrt(x^2+y^2) must match the fitted visibility (Bonferroni over 36), r<=1.1. SX: observed z^2+y^2 versus the model value (Bonferroni over 16).

drop_longest.threshold_justification: nested-estimator difference z = diff / sqrt(SE_dropped^2 - SE_full^2) (Wald SEs, floor 0.2 SE_full), |z| > Bonferroni z over 16 parameters at alpha 0.005 (3.60). With m=8 (CZ) or m=24 (SX) removed the dropped fit has less leverage, so only a large, significant shift indicates the longest repetition drives the result.
